specs.anchorText: Neither is "more correct"; each declares which transformations it agrees to ignore.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette: two identical twin cartoon photographs of the same smiling cat side by side, one in normal daylight and the other bathed in bright sunshine so it looks much lighter overall. A fussy little robot inspector (representing SSD) frowns and holds up a big red cross, fooled by the brightness difference. A calm, relaxed robot inspector (representing NCC) wearing sunglasses gives a cheerful thumbs up and a green check, completely unbothered by the lighting because it mentally subtracts the glare. The two robots stand between the two cat photos. Style is friendly and approachable like a comic strip or XKCD-inspired infographic, expressive characters, minimal clutter, clean very light background, generous margins. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. One clear visual metaphor.
specs.alt: Two photos of the same cat, one brighter than the other; a fussy SSD robot rejects the match with a red cross while a relaxed sunglasses-wearing NCC robot approves it with a green check, illustrating that a matching score is a choice of which changes, like lighting, to ignore.
specs.caption: A match score is a promise about what you agree to ignore: SSD ignores nothing and panics at a suntan, while normalized cross-correlation shrugs the brightness off.

specs.anchorText: a detector that says "no person" everywhere would score near-perfect accuracy while finding nobody

But the robot's eyes are closed and it has confidently stamped every single window of the scene, including all the obvious people, with a small REJECT-style red stamp that reads as a simple cross mark, so it has actually found nobody at all. One cartoon pedestrian behind it raises an eyebrow and points, unimpressed. The humor is the gap between the robot's pride and its uselessness. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. One clear visual metaphor.
specs.alt: A smug robot detector with its eyes closed proudly holds a near-perfect-score trophy while having stamped every window of a crowded street, including all the obvious pedestrians, with a red cross meaning no person, so it found nobody, illustrating why high accuracy is meaningless when background windows vastly outnumber objects.
specs.caption: Answer no person to every window and you score almost perfectly while finding nobody, which is exactly why detection counts the misses, not the hits.
